claims.text: The target material is a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with nominal composition TaVCrW.
Replacing the liquid-state EAM potential with an MTP can substantially reduce the cost of evaluating phase free energies and fusion properties in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Using FEP instead of full ab initio thermodynamic integration can substantially reduce computational cost while maintaining high accuracy.
An MTP can be trained for the liquid phase with an error below 1 meV/atom.
The MTP accurately reproduces the ab initio phase-space distribution of a multicomponent alloy.
Liquid configurations sampled with the MTP closely match configurations sampled by full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The variance of MTP-to-DFT energy differences is small enough for efficient free-energy perturbation.
Minimizing the variance of MTP-to-DFT energy differences accelerates convergence of free-energy calculations.
The MTP-FEP workflow retains electronic Gibbs-energy contributions associated with a density-of-states gap at the Fermi level.
Solid-state short-range order provides approximately 2.4 meV/atom of stabilization.
The proposed method will reduce computational resource usage by approximately 80% relative to the original TOR-TILD method.
The proposed method will provide approximately a 20-fold speedup relative to the original TOR-TILD method.
MTP-FEP free-energy differences will converge to within 0.5 meV/atom of full ab initio thermodynamic-integration results.
Electronic excitation effects will shift the melting temperature by approximately 48–57 K.
The method is expected to work for BCC TaVCrW at 0 GPa over 2000–2400 K.
The workflow can be applied to supercells of approximately 3456 atoms corresponding to 12×12×12 unit cells.
Magnetic fluctuations are negligible under the proposed high-temperature test conditions.
Exchange-correlation discrepancies may be especially important for V and Cr.

contradictions.description: An 80% reduction in resource usage corresponds to roughly a 5-fold speedup for equal work, not a 20-fold speedup. A 20-fold speedup would correspond to approximately a 95% reduction.
